title: Check generated variant registration and callers before reproducing a local anomaly
applies_when: A candidate comes from a partial window of generated, shape- or dtype-specialized kernel code, especially a low-level binding, reusable helper or host wrapper with separate autotuning and execution paths.
lesson: Retrieve the package registry and host dtype/shape dispatch before treating one physical kernel as the public API contract. Trace a requested output dtype through allocation, autotuner eligibility and the launch argument: agreeing buffer allocation alone does not prove these stages agree. Read the downstream validator before calling a mismatch memory corruption; it may reject the call before JIT. Trace the suspected helper to an actual call, and substitute the specialized dimensions into padding/index arithmetic. A bf16-only binding can be correct for its registered key; a constant-false padding branch can be harmless when the dimension is already aligned; an unused helper does not establish an active ordering bug. Equal shared-memory offsets can describe different producer and consumer views of the same data, not independent buffers overwriting each other. Follow actual pointer uses, including lowered numeric offsets, and synchronization before deciding; macro names alone may have no downstream references. These checks can refute a particular premise without compiling its target environment.
avoid_when: Do not exclude all generated code or assume an unregistered shape is necessarily acceptable API behavior. A shared quantization kind need not imply symmetric weight/activation storage: MXFP4/MXFP8 can use packed FP4 weights with unpacked E4M3 activations. Read the role-specific dtype/shape table and staging allocation before borrowing another role's unpacking path. Reopen with a supported logical key routed to the wrong variant, a reachable consumer of unwritten bytes, or a real helper call and compiler/runtime evidence. Static reachability and arithmetic are not native numerical correctness, performance or portability tests.

evidence.note: The W4A4 host pipeline allocates the requested output dtype but passes a literal BF16 GEMM2 launch dtype. The tuner independently uses BF16 for eligibility; checking just one stage misses the mismatch.
The downstream wrapper rejects a provided output with the wrong dtype before kernel compilation. The source mismatch does not by itself establish memory corruption.

Scoped CPU metadata regression: three FP16 checks failed while three BF16 controls passed; aligning launch and eligibility dtype passed six checks. Real Torch buffers and real can_implement checks, kernel execution mocked. Existing author already fixes execution; this contributes the remaining tuner finding, not native GPU correctness or performance.

KERNELS maps architecture and logical dtype/shape/fold keys to physical generated modules. kernel_module_name rejects missing keys before loading a binding; the two inspected K8192 folded quantizers are bf16 keys, not shared fp16 implementations.

prepare_nvfp4_per_token_quantize derives the logical key from the actual input dtype. padded_sf_cols and the fixed K=8192 generated quantizer explain why a scale-column padding branch can be empty without missing required columns.

The suspect mbarrier_wait_relaxed_hint appears only as a definition in this complete translation unit, not a call or address reference. This is a scoped counterexample to inferring an active wait-ordering bug from the helper window alone.

The TMA producer writes SFB via smem_v3..v6 addresses; after waiting on tma_full, the MMA role reads scale descriptors via the larger smem_v7/v8 views. Their equal base offsets are used in the same kernel, not mutually exclusive variants. The macros themselves appear only as definitions; actual operands use pointer variables and lowered numbers. This contradicts the premise that simultaneous use of equal offsets necessarily means independent-buffer overwrite, not a native numerical or complete synchronization-safety qualification.

The mixed mxfp4_mxfp8 kind maps activation storage to E4M3 with per-32 E8M0 scales. Its role-specific properties and workspace retain full hidden-width activations, while weight shapes use half width. This contradicts inferring packed FP4 activations from packed weights; it is not a native SM107 kernel qualification.

The activation helper converts FP8 values directly and the weight helper unpacks FP4 for the same mixed kind. This asymmetry agrees with the bound storage contract; native CPU helper checks are not a whole-package/GPU or cross-format correctness claim.

The supported DSA host entry enforces head/token/key-row strides modulo eight BF16 elements and base alignment modulo 16 bytes before architecture-specific binding selection. A generated whole-byte-offset check need not duplicate this complete contract; distinguish bits-to-bytes representability from TMA alignment. This refutes an external-input bypass premise, not every directly invoked raw binding or internal backward layout.

Existing host-validator tests cover legal trainer-strided layouts and rejected unsupported strides/base alignment. These publicly reviewable controls support reading the complete caller contract before reproducing a generated binding anomaly; they do not establish full native GPU correctness.
